event_overview.title: About FAA Resumes Flights After Nationwide Ground Stop Due to System Overload
event_overview.subject: FAA Resumes Flights After Nationwide Ground Stop Due to System Overload
event_overview.summary: On November 13, 2026, the Federal Aviation Administration imposed a nationwide ground stop for U.S. airports after communications problems affected multiple air-route traffic-control centers. The restriction was a precaution taken amid intermittent telecommunications outages that impaired the stability of air-traffic-control communications and radar; the FAA subsequently cancelled the stop and began restoring departures.

facts.label: Date and duration
facts.value: The disruption began on Friday, November 13, 2026. The Department of Transportation said airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time; the FAA Command Center’s cancellation advisory was issued shortly after 01:19 UTC on November 14.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The FAA applied the ground stop to all U.S. airports, after communication issues affected multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

facts.label: Stated safety rationale
facts.value: DOT said the FAA acted out of caution because intermittent telecommunications outages were affecting the stability of communications and radar used by air traffic control.

facts.label: Operational cause under investigation
facts.value: Officials said data inconsistencies arose as legacy switches and routers were overloaded; the FAA’s initial statement characterized the information as preliminary and said technicians were investigating.

facts.label: How a national ground stop works
facts.value: FAA procedures require evaluation of less restrictive measures where possible, coordination across affected facilities and system users, and an advisory describing the national restriction; flights subject to a ground stop are held at their departure points.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the November 13–14, 2026 nationwide stop and the resumption of flight operations; it does not attempt to catalogue every airline cancellation, airport-level delay, or subsequent investigation update.

related_events.title: Airlines Face Major Disruptions Following Nationwide Ground Stop
related_events.summary: Airlines in the US are working to recover from a nationwide ground stop that lasted over four hours on Friday, resulting in the cancellation of more than 2,000 flights. The disruption has caused significant delays and stranded passengers, impacting travel plans across the country and internationally. Professional and college sports teams have also been affected, seeking alternative transportation options.
